instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows. Pause briefly near the bottom, then press through your palms to return to the starting position. Keep your core braced throughout.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out. Brace your core and push your hips back as you bend your knees. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive through your heels to stand back up. Keep your chest lifted and knees tracking over your toes.

Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders. Extend your legs behind you and form a straight line from head to heels. Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes. Hold the position without letting your hips sag or rise too high.

muscle_groups_activated: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps, Rear Delts, Upper Back
instructions: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away. Start from a dead hang with shoulders engaged. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving elbows down and back. Lower yourself under control to a full hang.

Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level. Press the weights upward until your arms are extended but not locked. Lower the dumbbells slowly until your elbows are just below bench level. Keep your feet planted and shoulder blades retracted.

Stand with feet hip-width apart and the bar over the midfoot. Hinge at the hips, bend your knees, and grip the bar just outside your legs. Keep your back flat and chest up as you drive through the floor to stand tall. Lower the bar by pushing your hips back first, then bending your knees.

Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor. Keep your front knee aligned over your ankle. Push through the front heel to return to standing, then repeat on the other side.

Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the bar at upper chest height. Tighten your core and glutes. Press the bar overhead in a straight path until your arms are fully extended. Lower it back to the starting position under control.

Hold a barbell with an overhand grip and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is near parallel to the floor. Keep a neutral spine and knees slightly bent. Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower the bar slowly without rounding your back.

Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Sit your hips down and back as you squat, keeping your chest tall. Drive through your heels to stand back up.

Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width and the kettlebell a foot or so in front of you. Hinge at the hips to grab the kettlebell and hike it back between your legs. Explosively extend your hips to swing it to chest height. Let the bell return naturally and repeat using a hip hinge, not a squat.

Stand tall and take a controlled step forward into a lunge. Lower your back knee toward the floor while keeping your torso upright. Push through the front heel to bring the back leg forward into the next step. Continue alternating legs as you move forward.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Keep your arms at your sides. Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.

Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs and knees slightly bent. Push your hips back while keeping the weights close to your legs and your back neutral. Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings. Drive your hips forward to stand back up.

muscle_groups_activated: Lats, Biceps, Rear Delts, Upper Back
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pads. Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest while keeping your torso stable. Slowly return the bar overhead with control.

Sit with your feet on the platform and grab the handle. Keep your chest up and spine neutral. Pull the handle toward your torso by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades. Extend your arms slowly to return to the start.

Sit in the leg press machine with your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. Release the safety handles and lower the sled until your knees bend comfortably. Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking the knees. Keep your lower back against the seat.

Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest. Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles. Press forward until your arms are nearly extended. Return the handles slowly until your elbows are bent and your chest is stretched.

Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and raise the weights out to the sides until they reach shoulder height. Lower them slowly with control. Avoid swinging or shrugging.

Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing forward. Keep your elbows close to your sides. Curl the weights toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms. Lower them slowly to full extension.

Stand facing a high pulley with a rope or straight bar attachment. Keep your elbows tucked at your sides. Push the handle down until your arms are fully extended. Return slowly until your forearms are just above parallel to the floor.

Sit in the leg extension machine and place your shins behind the pad. Grip the handles and extend your knees to lift the weight. Pause briefly at the top, then lower the pad slowly. Keep your hips down against the seat.

Lie face down on the hamstring curl machine and position the pad just above your heels. Curl your heels toward your glutes by bending your knees. Squeeze at the top, then lower the weight with control. Keep your hips pressed into the bench.

Stand on the calf raise platform with the balls of your feet on the edge. Lower your heels as far as comfortable to get a full stretch. Rise onto your toes as high as possible. Pause briefly at the top and lower slowly.

Kneel facing a high cable with a rope attachment held near your temples. Keep your hips still and round your upper spine as you crunch your ribs toward your pelvis. Exhale as you contract your abs. Return slowly to the start without using momentum.

Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs as if running in place. Keep your hips low and your core tight. Maintain a fast but controlled rhythm.

Stand tall, then squat down and place your hands on the floor. Jump your feet back into a plank and optionally lower into a push-up. Jump your feet back toward your hands and explode upward with a small jump. Land softly and repeat.
Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides. Jump your feet out while raising your arms overhead. Jump back to the starting position. Keep the movement light and rhythmic.

Stand tall and begin jogging in place while driving your knees up toward hip height. Swing your arms naturally to help maintain pace. Land softly on the balls of your feet. Keep your torso upright and core engaged.

Hold the rope handles and stand with feet together. Rotate the rope using your wrists and make small jumps as it passes under your feet. Land softly on the balls of your feet. Keep your jumps low and consistent.

Stand in front of a sturdy box with feet shoulder-width apart. Dip slightly at the hips and swing your arms to generate momentum. Jump onto the box and land softly with both feet fully on top. Step down carefully and repeat.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a medicine ball overhead. Engage your core and forcefully slam the ball into the floor using your upper body and hips. Squat down to pick it up safely. Repeat with explosive effort.

Hold a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand at your sides. Stand tall with shoulders back and core braced. Walk forward with controlled steps while maintaining posture. Keep the weights from swinging excessively.

Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell over your hips. Plant your feet shoulder-width apart. Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

Hold dumbbells at your sides and stand in front of a box or bench. Place one foot firmly on the surface and drive through that heel to step up. Bring the other leg up with control, then step back down. Alternate legs or complete all reps on one side before switching.

Place your hands on a bench, box, or elevated surface and extend your legs behind you. Keep your body straight from head to heels. Lower your chest toward the surface by bending your elbows. Press back up to the starting position.

Kneel on the assistance pad or use the counterweight setting on a dip machine. Grip the handles and support yourself with straight arms. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press back up until your arms are extended.

Sit at the pec deck machine and place your forearms or hands against the pads. Keep a slight bend in your elbows. Bring the handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your pectoral muscles. Return slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest.

muscle_groups_activated: Rear Delts, Upper Back, Traps, Rotator Cuff
instructions: Set a rope attachment at upper chest or face height. Pull the rope toward your face while separating your hands and keeping elbows high. Squeeze your upper back at the end of the movement. Return slowly with control.

Hinge at the hips with a flat back and let the dumbbells hang beneath your shoulders. With a slight bend in the elbows, raise the weights out to the sides. Squeeze your shoulder blades gently together. Lower slowly without jerking.

Kneel on the floor and hold the ab wheel under your shoulders. Brace your core and roll forward slowly, extending your arms as far as you can while maintaining a neutral spine. Pause briefly, then pull back to the starting position using your abs and lats. Avoid letting your lower back arch.

Stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front of you. Reach your arms forward for balance and lower into a single-leg squat as far as mobility allows. Keep the working foot flat and the knee aligned. Drive through the heel to stand back up.

Lie on a bench holding a barbell with arms extended above your chest. Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind it. Keep your upper arms steady throughout the movement. Extend your elbows to press the bar back up.

Sit back on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging at your sides. Curl the weights upward while keeping your upper arms still. Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch. Avoid swinging your torso.

Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder level. Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles. Press upward until your arms are nearly straight. Lower the weight with control to shoulder height.

Position your hips on the back extension bench and secure your feet. Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head. Hinge at the hips to lower your torso, then extend your back and hips to return to a straight line. Avoid hyperextending at the top.

Load a sled appropriately and place your hands on the poles. Lean your body forward at an angle and drive through the floor to push the sled. Keep your torso rigid and steps short and powerful. Continue for the desired distance.

Start in a high plank position with a dumbbell in each hand. Keep your feet wider than hip-width for stability. Row one dumbbell toward your ribcage while resisting rotation through the torso. Lower it and repeat on the other side.

Stand with your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent around 90 degrees. Keep your feet flat and knees over ankles. Hold the position while maintaining an upright torso. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

Sit on the rowing machine with feet secured and hold the handle. Begin with the drive by pushing through your legs, then lean back slightly and pull the handle toward your lower ribs. Reverse the motion by extending your arms, then hinging forward, then bending your knees. Maintain a smooth, rhythmic stroke.
